review_type: unblinded static contract review, separate from frozen behavioral grading
scope: Read complete baseline and candidate propose-design/discuss instructions and the complete unchanged frame-problem/vault-search dependencies. Compared top-level frontmatter, fenced blocks and final candidate copies by exact content. No repository, fixture or candidate mutation.
verdict: No concrete unintended lost requirement found. The candidate preserves the reviewed contract while making the stated intentional clarification and authorization changes.

contract_assessments.evidence: Both edited skills have byte-identical top-level frontmatter, including their names and activation descriptions. propose-design retains its one YAML block; discuss retains both YAML blocks byte-for-byte. Candidate copies match the final repository skill files.
contract_assessments.limits: This verifies textual identity, not activation quality or a live schema validator.

contract_assessments.evidence: Candidate propose-design lines 14–20 retain topic search before drafting; no match chains to frame-problem; one draft or accepted match becomes the frame; obsolete framing requires explaining it was set aside and asking about a successor or another frame; multiple matches require user selection with ids, statuses and titles. Lines 25–28 retain incoming frames edge lookup and distinction between alternatives, successors and different work.
contract_assessments.limits: Multiple matches were not dynamically exercised.

contract_assessments.requirement: Required frame and explicit no-frame exception
contract_assessments.evidence: Candidate propose-design lines 22–23 require frames and retain explicit user request, free-text reason and one pushback before frames: none. The unchanged activation text also states the exception. Consolidation removes the repeated prohibition without weakening its explicit exception.
contract_assessments.limits: The no-frame exception was statically reviewed only.

contract_assessments.evidence: Candidate propose-design lines 18–19 explicitly direct superseding through frame-problem. That unchanged dependency includes obsolete-frame warning/supersession, a supersedes field, and accepted problem immutability. The abbreviated parent clause does not introduce an edit-in-place route.
Candidate propose-design lines 27–28 expressly forbid editing accepted designs and require a new brief with supersedes: <old-id>. Both supplied execution cases left prior artifacts byte-identical.

Candidate propose-design lines 55–67 retain the opening approach paragraph before subsections; rationale tied to named constraints; concrete APIs/schemas/workflows/layouts/sequences with examples preferred; effort, risks, compatibility effects and participants plus how to enable unknown estimates; two or three rejected alternatives including doing nothing where viable; and conditions for abandonment or supersession. The instruction to reference rather than repeat the problem remains.
contract_assessments.limits: Compression changes wording such as what it breaks to compatibility effects; risks remain explicit, so this is not a concrete omission of cost/risk analysis.

contract_assessments.requirement: Diff presentation, filenames and commit paths
contract_assessments.evidence: Candidate propose-design lines 50–51 retain briefs/<id>.md, creation date, no -design suffix; lines 76 and 80–81 retain filename/frontmatter/body diff and scoped Design commit command. discuss lines 52, 92 and 97–98 retain discussions/<id>.md, diff and Note commit command. Discussion/session-note suffixes and metadata remain in unchanged schema blocks.

Candidate propose-design lines 82–87 require the checker before requested proposed/accepted promotion, resolving blockers before promotion, separate promotion authorization, accurate state/blocker reporting, and record-decision with derived_from. The unchanged vault-search dependency still requires checks before proposing status changes. Consolidating duplicate reminders did not remove the gate.
contract_assessments.limits: Only a blocked fixture acceptance was executed. Successful promotion and real validator behavior remain untested.

contract_assessments.requirement: Discussion types, body, no invented participants/decisions
contract_assessments.evidence: Candidate discuss retains the two note flavors, no attendees for solo session notes, both schemas, loose context/attributed-summary/open-question/followup body guidance, and the explicit no-invented-attendees-or-decisions rule at lines 124–125.

Candidate discuss lines 69–83 retain search for each implication and the six-row routing table: problem, design, decision, inquiry, supersession and arc closure. The instruction to present choices and not chain automatically is unchanged; workflow lines 99–100 also retain triage.

Candidate discuss lines 104–125 retain no direct transitions from discuss, documenting implications, proposing followups, obtaining go-ahead, checking transitions and presenting blockers before phase-skill/manual handling. No status field may be assigned to either note type.

Candidate propose-design lines 71–75 explicitly reuse supplied answers, ask only consequential missing information including authorship and mark user-requested draft gaps. Candidate discuss lines 87–89 use supplied author/participant/solo context and ask only missing details. These replace generic questioning or reconfirmation with the instructed behavior.

Candidate propose-design lines 76–79 and discuss lines 93–96 proceed with an already authorized write/commit, otherwise obtain approval, and carry applicable authorization from calling skills such as plan-feature. The language remains scoped to the brief/note and does not authorize unrelated work.
Candidate discuss line 96 explicitly says note authorization does not authorize followups, reinforcing the unchanged user-choice and status-transition gates.

observed_execution_schema_followup.candidate_design: The produced candidate design contains id/type/draft status/author/created/frames/scopes/supersedes/relates_to/conflicts_with/depends_on/tags; arc is legitimately omitted by the unchanged template. Its date-based filename and substantive body match the contract.
observed_execution_schema_followup.candidate_session_note: The produced candidate note contains the session-suffixed id/type/author/created/scopes/relates_to, with optional arc omitted and no status/attendees.
observed_execution_schema_followup.baseline_difference: Baseline outputs omit scopes while candidate outputs use scopes: []. The schema text itself is unchanged; this execution variation is not a candidate contract regression. The frozen blind grading is unchanged.

limits: Static review establishes instruction preservation, not broad behavioral reliability.
Calling-skill authorization, multiple frame selection, explicit frames: none, missing design authorship, and successful promotion are not all exercised by the six cases.
Dependency content identity does not prove workers read those files; worker-reported reads remain uninstrumented.
No claim that unchanged activation or schemas improve activation/schema-validation quality is supported.
Existing discuss ordering language (draft then triage, alongside a search-first dependency) is unchanged; the review does not claim to resolve all pre-existing instruction tensions.
